title: Putting Commuters First in Public Transport
what_it_is: Putting Commuters First in Public Transport

sections.label: Train reliability MKBF improvement
sections.summary: MKBF improved from 180,000 to 661,000 train/km between 2017 and the first three quarters of 2018, with a one million train/km target by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With these investments, we have seen Mean Kilometres Between Failures (MKBF) improve from 180,000 train/kilometres (km) to 661,000 train/km between 2017 and the first three quarters of 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With a new reliability target of one million train/km by 2020, it may appear that our train reliability is on the up.

sections.label: 2018 fare hike and NCF
sections.summary: The 2018 exercise first used the revised Fare Review Formula with a Network Capacity Factor, and the first fare hike hitting the 4.3% cap drew negative responses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The 2018 exercise saw the first use of the revised Fare Review Formula with a new component known as the Network Capacity Factor (NCF), and the first fare hike which hit the cap of 4.3% in over three years drew many negative responses from citizens.

sections.label: Fare hikes impact on disadvantaged groups
sections.summary: SMRT and SBS Transit must transfer 5% of added fare revenue to the Public Transport Fund, but the impact of fare hikes on disadvantaged groups needs watching.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For now, I note in passing that, even as SMRT and Singapore Bus Services (SBS) Transit are mandated to transfer 5% of the added fare revenue to the Public Transport Fund that funds subsidy vouchers for vulnerable groups, we must maintain a vigilant watch on the impact of such fare hikes on our disadvantaged groups, especially the groups that still prefer cash transactions that saw the highest fare hikes.

sections.label: Additional MKBF incident categories
sections.summary: The speaker suggests having other MKBF categories for all incidents, such as less than five minutes, between five and 30 minutes, and more than 30 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Beyond and alongside the traditional measure of MKBF for more than five minutes only, I would suggest having other categories of MKBF for all incidents, such as less than five minutes, between five and 30 minutes and more than 30 minutes.

sections.label: Third-party evaluators in Fare Review
sections.summary: Third-party evaluators like ISE could provide less biased scores, which could be factored into the Fare Review formula to reward positive commuter experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps third-party evaluators like ISE which run independent surveys can provide a picture less likely to draw accusations of bias.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Such independently derived scores can then be directly factored into the Fare Review formula where positive commuter experiences should be rewarded while stagnant or negative commuter experience should be a factor against fare increases.

sections.label: PTO profits in Fare Review formula
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering including the profits of public transport operators as one factor in the Fare Review formula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My second point, also related to the topic of fare review, is that we ought to consider including the profits of PTOs as one factor in the Fare Review formula.

sections.label: Hong Kong MTR fare formula
sections.summary: Hong Kong's Fare Adjustment Mechanism includes MTR Corporation profits within the productivity factor, defined as Hong Kong transport revenue divided by Hong Kong transport expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Hong Kong’s formula for adjusting their Mass Transit Railway (MTR) fares, the Fare Adjustment Mechanism (FAM), the profits of the MTR Corporation are set within the factor of productivity, where "productivity" is revenue from the corporation's Hong Kong transport operations divided by its expenses relating to its Hong Kong transport operations.

sections.label: Public Transport Fund subsidy transfer
sections.summary: Currently 5% of additional fare revenues earned by public transport operators are transferred to the Public Transport Fund to subsidise vulnerable groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, 5% of additional fare revenues earned by the PTOs are transferred to the Public Transport Fund to subsidise vulnerable groups.

sections.label: Rail renewal plans and milestones
sections.summary: The Government must have renewal plans, with major North-East Line works starting 2019, and the speaker calls for major rail renewals every 15-year milestone under the new framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To not repeat past mistakes, the Government must have renewal plans in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, glad to note that there will be major enhancement and renewal works for the North-East Line starting in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With this in mind, I would like to call on the Government to commit to major renewals for rail assets under the new Rail Financing Framework at every 15-year milestone.

sections.label: Profits in Fare Review formula
sections.summary: The second proposal is to include the profits of public transport operators as one factor in the Fare Review formula.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, include the profits of PTOs as one factor in the Fare Review formula.

sections.label: Workers' Party rail renewal call
sections.summary: The Workers' Party urges the Government to commit to major rail asset renewals every 15 years under the New Rail Financing Framework, and says more work remains on commuter experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fifth, the Workers' Party urge the Government to commit to major renewals for rail assets every 15 years under the New Rail Financing Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is still work to do in improving our public transportation system, particularly in providing better commuter experiences in areas, such as reliability, affordability and quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: (In English) In closing, we should refrain on patting ourselves on the back on our current progress in our public transportation system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is still work to do in improving our public transportation system, particularly in putting our commuters first over other stakeholders in areas, such as reliability, affordability and quality.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: I got a bit more worried because he went on to congratulate us for 13 straight years of public transport ridership growth and we are quite proud of that.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: He confirmed that our reliability has improved on a regular basis, in fact, exceeding expectations, to 670,000 MKBF when we have set ourselves a target of 400,000 MKBF for this year.

sections.label: Bus and rail financing models
sections.summary: Another mechanism is the model used, with the transition to the Bus Contracting Model in 2016 and the new Rail Financing Framework in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Another mechanism is the model that we use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We transitioned to the Bus Contracting Model in 2016, the new Rail Financing Framework in 2018.

sections.label: Fares decline over five years
sections.summary: Over the last five years, fares have gone down by 1.2%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, fares have gone down by 1.2%.

sections.label: Wages rise in that time
sections.summary: In that time, wages have risen by 17.7%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In that time, wages have risen by 17.7%.

sections.label: Commuters on concession schemes
sections.summary: 1.8 million commuters are on some form of concession schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Less well-known is the fact that 1.8 million commuters are on some form of concession schemes.

sections.label: Concession commuters and improvements
sections.summary: 1.8 million daily public transport users benefit from concession schemes, had a one-cent increase, and reliability, affordability and inclusivity improved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Out of our population, 1.8 million of the people who regularly use public transport on a daily basis are already benefiting from the concession schemes that we have.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: They had an even lower increase in the last fare review that Mr Dennis Tan was talking about, at only one cent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As a result, reliability has improved, affordability has improved, inclusivity has improved.
